Small town bakery marks fifty years on the same corner
Staff reporter
The bakery on the corner of Elm and Fourth has been run by the same family since it opened its doors five decades ago, and the ovens in the back room are the same ones installed on opening day, kept running through regular repairs rather than replacement.
Regulars say the shop has barely changed inside, from the hand painted sign in the window to the wooden counter worn smooth by generations of customers leaning on it while they waited for their order to come out of the oven.
The current owner, grandson of the founder, says he has no plans to modernize the recipes or the decor, arguing that consistency is exactly what keeps people coming back decade after decade, even as chain bakeries have opened and closed nearby.
He does admit that the till is no longer a hand crank cash register, which broke beyond repair three years ago and was quietly replaced with a card reader, the one concession to modern life the shop has allowed itself.
